standard_text: The Earth is a planet that spins on its axis (day and night) and moves around the Sun. The Sun is a star that gives light and heat. The Moon moves around the Earth and seems to change shape (phases). Rockets are systems that carry things into space. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 4, Planet Earth and Beyond: Planet Earth; the Sun; the Earth and the Sun; the Moon)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology worksheets (CAPS): the Earth, the Sun, day and night, the Moon and its phases, and rockets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The Earth spins once a day and orbits the Sun once a year.
key_sub: The Moon shines by reflecting sunlight.
body_html:
How to think about it

The Earth is a ball-shaped planet. It spins on its axis once every 24 hours: the side facing the Sun has day and the other side has night. The Earth moves around the Sun once a year. The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot gas that gives us light and heat.

The Moon moves around the Earth about once a month. It does not make its own light: we see the part lit by the Sun, so its shape seems to change from new moon to full moon. Rockets push hot gases backwards to move forwards into space.

Example

Why is it night in Durban while it is day on the other side of the world?

Earth spins.

Answer: the Earth's rotation

Example

Does the Moon make its own light?

Think of a mirror.

Answer: no, it reflects sunlight

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun moves around the Earth.
  • Thinking the Moon's phases are caused by the Earth's shadow.
  • Thinking the Sun is a planet.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the full moon?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: Why don't eclipses happen every month?
c: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so the Sun, Earth and Moon rarely line up exactly.

items.q: What happens in a lunar eclipse?

The Sun passes in front of the Moon.
